Guidance & outlook: Consequently, the total cost of Fly Ash consumed during FY 2025-26 stood at ₹1,661.48 lakhs, as against ₹1,944.17 lakhs in FY 2024-25.

(iii) Packing bags: During FY 2025-26, the Company consumed 63.83 lakh packing bags at an average acquisition cost of ₹11.47 per bag, compared with 62.40 lakh packing bags at an average acquisition cost of ₹11.23 per bag during FY 2024-25.

(b) Salaries, Wages and Labor Cost During FY 2025-26, the Company incurred ₹2,168.25 lakhs towards Employee benefit expenses in form of salaries, wages and labour costs, as compared to ₹1,891.00 lakhs in FY 2024-25, representing an increase of ₹277.25 lakhs (approximately 14.66%).
Growth & demand: Although fluctuations in fuel prices, logistics costs and raw material prices remained areas of concern, the long-term demand outlook for the cement industry continues to remain positive, supported by sustained infrastructure investments, rapid urbanisation and increasing housing demand.

The Government's continued focus on infrastructure-led development is expected to remain a key driver of cement demand over the coming years, providing favourable growth opportunities for the Company and the industry as a whole.
These structural advantages are expected to support sustained demand across core sectors, including cement, thereby creating long-term growth opportunities for the industry.
Margins & costs: 30.2 Cost Auditors and Cost Audit Report Pursuant to Section 148 of the Companies Act, 2013 read with the Companies (Cost Records and Audit) Amendment Rules, 2014, the cost records maintained by the Company in respect of its manufacturing activity are required to be audited.

COSTS (a) Raw Material (i) Lime Stone: The Company consumed 2,34,941.60 MT of Limestone during FY 2025-26, compared with 2,17,541.62 MT in the previous year, representing an increase of approximately 8.0%.

(d) Financial Costs During FY 2025-26, the Company incurred ₹421.59 lakhs towards Interest and Financial Costs, as compared to ₹555.62 lakhs in FY 2024-25, representing a decrease of ₹134.03 lakhs (approximately 24.12%).
Capex & expansion: India continues to be the second-largest cement producer globally, with installed cement manufacturing capacity exceeding 650 million tonnes per annum.

Industry participants continued to invest in capacity expansion, operational efficiencies, renewable energy, waste heat recovery systems and alternative fuels to improve competitiveness and sustainability.
The consumption of packing bags increased by 1.43 lakh bags (approximately 2.29%), while the average acquisition cost increased by ₹0.24 per bag (approximately 2.14%).
Balance sheet & cash: The Company has transferred the unpaid or unclaimed dividends declared up to the financial years 2011-12, from time to time on due dates to the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF) established by the Central Government.

DIVIDEND The Board of Directors of the Company after considering the financial and non-financial factors prevailing during the financial year 2025-26 decided not to recommend any dividend for the financial year 2025-26.

Risks & challenges: RISK MANAGEMENT Risk is an integral and unavoidable component of business and Company's risk management process is designed to identify and mitigate risks that have the potential to materially impact its business objectives and maintains a balance between managing risk and making most of the opportunities.
While inflationary pressures moderated in several advanced economies, growth continued to be uneven due to supply chain disruptions, regional conflicts and volatile commodity prices.
However, risks arising from geopolitical developments, energy price volatility, global financial market uncertainty and protectionist trade policies continue to warrant close monitoring.
